STOCK THEFT 2.0

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Live Stock Theft taken to whole new level with a sophisticated scam run from within a Free State Prison.

Unique Selling Point:
An unusual con with a twist....

An opportunity to throw the spotlight on the weaknesses with in Correctional Services - I did the Waterkloof 4 story at least 3 years ago when we showed the extent of cellphones in prisons - but it's gone next level with criminals not only having access to the outside world - but are running extensive cons from inside.

Summary:
Times are tough in the farming industry. The economy and the climate has taken it’s toll on many farmers, with more and more farms up for sale.

A conman is exploiting their desperation – pretending to buy farms using stolen details and fake proof of payments only to steal their livestock.

Sound like a straightforward con? But there’s twist. The crook is already behind bars – he’s running the scam from inside the Kroonstad Prison.

Further information:
THE CON
The Farming community has become the playground of a very inventive conman. He’s knowledgable and sounds like older, Afrikaans farmer who knows the business and speaks the lingo.

The Conman responds to For Sale ads for farms and livestock. He makes an offer, signs the offer to purchases with comprehensive details and sends through a proof of payment. He’ll send through a foreman to inspect the farm while the deal is going on making it seem legit. Then he’ll want to move the livestock and starts making arrangements. Often he’s dealing with farmers in areas that have bad cellphone reception or where the farmers aren’t physically on the land. A livestock transporter will arrive and make off with the livestock – it’s either sold at an auction or to butchery or another farmer. Before you know you know it, the animals are gone and there is no sign of the money in your bank account.

The foreman & transporter are NOT part of the con – they have ALSO been conned! They don’t get payment for their services and are left out of pocket.

Farmers have been targeted across SA – from the Free State, to the Northern Cape to the Eastern Cape.

If you look at the proof of payments – you can find problems with it if you compare it to an original one from the bank – issues around layout and spelling.

SO WHO IS THE CON?
Well he uses different aliases – usually the name of the previous farmer he scammed because during the sale process he would have gotten all the details – ID’s, contact addresses, etc. So when the new mark dues his due diligence – there will be a legitimate person, who is in the farming industry by that name usually with other properties on their name.

The con is a man by the name of Joseph Nguro. He grew up on farms in the Free State and is currently serving a sentence in the Kroonstad Prison for fraud and stock theft. His old MO was to physically cut fences and steal live stock. There is another 9 cases using his original MO currently running in court where he is linked.

With his new MO there are 27 cases being investigated linked back to Joseph. The police’s Stock Theft Unit is making progress but they are frustrated with Correctional Services – the prisoner is able to run an elaborate con from his jail cell using mobile phones.

HOW DO WE DO IT?
We have access to a number of voice recordings of the con making arrangement to buy the farms and move the animals. All the recording from the different scams are the same voice.

We will be able to shoot re-enactment of the animals being loaded – so visually we’ll have creative overlay.

AND THEN ☺
We can post an ad for a farm with livestock – pretending that my father passed away and that I need to sell quite quickly. That way we’ll get our own recordings, and we’ll be able to trace the cell numbers ourselves to link it back to the suspect. We could even get Devi to call him and call him out on the con.

CASE STUDIES
CASE STUDY 1
Bennie Smit from Stompiesfontein in the Calvinia District received an offer to purchase his farm and the livestock on the farm. His estate agent and lawyers said it looked legit. The new buyer wanted to move the sheep to another farm. 318 sheep was loaded. The value R318k – it was sold to a butcher in the Free State who says all the animals have been slaughtered. (We don’t need to go Calvinia – we can meet him Wolseley – it’s about 2 hours from Cape Town)

CASE STUDY 2
Gert Bekker got an offer to purchase from Jan Hendrik Potgieter. He pretend to buy the farm, made appointments to sign contracts, sent fake EFT-payments to Bekker and his lawyers and then started to move livestock, by the time Bekker realize that the proof of payment was fake, the livestock was long gone, but luckily in time to stop another shipment of livestock being loaded by the crooks

This is his story:
We had daily conversations. In short he decide to buy our farm as a running business with the exclusion of some of the livestock. Becker Bergh and More were assign to draw up the contracts for the running business and via e-mail the documents were sign. He (Jan Hendrik Potgieter) make arrangements to come to Upington on the 4th of July to sign the original contracts.

On 29th June 2017 he send proof of payments for the livestock (R1871 880.00) to me, and for the farm (R24 463 084.96) to Becker Bergh and More. He organize transport, with a local transporter, for the livestock on the 29th June and 1st July. When the money was not made available to my bank by the 1st of July, I suspect something was wrong and stop the second shipment of livestock.

CASE STUDY 3
THE REAL Jan Hendrik Potgieter was almost scammed in June. He dealt with the same conman pretending to be a Benjamin Nel. The crook arranged for cattle to be loaded – but fortunately for the real Jan – the auctioneers picked up something was amiss and they traced the animals back to him. His son-in-law has started a group for affected farmers and can give a good overview of the scam.

CASE STUDY 4
Raymond Daniels got offered a job as the foreman in one of these cons – he packed up his house, resigned from his job because of the brilliant offer he was made. He drove thousands of kilometres to the so-called farm and helped finalise arrangements for the transportation of livestock. He was left out of pocket, out of a job and had a lot of explaining to do to the angry farmer who initially thought he was part of con but only realised later Raymond was also a victim.

HIDDEN IDENTITY WITH RECENTLY RELEASED CONVICT
We’ll get an insiders perspective on how it works – how cellphones are smuggled in, how much it costs and just how rife it is in prisons across SA.

INTERVIEWS
• Correctional Services
• SAPS STOCK THEFT UNIT
• Case Studies
• Estate Agent / Lawyer that dealt with some of the deals to explain how legitimate everything looked.
• Hidden ID – ex-convict













Extra Budget Items:
An extra day with the presenter - we will need to do a lot of traveling around Gauteng to get the different case studies.

Wolseley, Skeerpoort, Carltonville

Press Release:


Stock Theft
Usually when a criminal is sentenced to serve time behind bars, that marks the end of his unlawful
activities. But one scamster has been running a sophisticated operation, stealing from desperate farmers -
seemingly from within his cell - inside Kroonstad Prison. From cattle, to sheep - livestock theft has been
taken to a whole new level. Carte Blanche investigates this cunning conman.

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Times are tough in the South African farming industry.

BENNIE: Ons sukkel op hierdie stadium jy kan se om kop bo water te bly.
ENGLISH: We are battling at this stage, you can say to keep our heads above water.

LINK: Economic and climatic conditions have resulted in more and more farms up for sale – but desperate times often opens to the door to conartists.

VO: At least 15 farmers have been scammed with fake deals totalling close to R2.5 million.

Bennie Smit and Riaan Lotz were contacted by a man wanting to buy their farms.

RIAAN: Hy het glad nie geknibble oor die prys nie.
ENGLISH: He didn’t argue about the price at all.

UPSOUND AUDIO RECORDING CLIP…. Man, I am looking for any farm, but it has to be a running concern, because look I am a cash buyer.

BENNIE: Daar’s nie twee stories – dis ‘n kontant koper. Joh dit kan nie beter gaan nie.
ENGLISH: There’s no two stories - it’s a cash buyer. Joh! It can’t go any better!
RIAAN: Hy’t gese hy is Jan Venter – hy is ‘n boer hy het voerkrale – hy is van Nelspruit en hy stel belang in my plaas.
ENGLISH: He said he is Jan Venter – he’s farmer with feeding pens. He’s from Nelspruit and he’s interested in my farm.

VO: Riaan & Bennie would only learn later on that the scam wasn’t actually about the sale of the farms – it was just a decoy.

After a year on the market – Riaan was happy with the offer for his game farm in Limpopo. But it wasn’t a done deal - the buyer wanted livestock on the farm.

RIAAN: Ek het hom probeer oorreed om te se jy kan die plaas as ‘n lopend saak koop, want daar is baie die wild op dit // – maar hy’t aanhou se – ek is ‘n bees man INT1 M7
ENGLISH: I tried to convince him that he can buy the farm as a going concern because there is a lot of game on it. But he kept saying – “I am a cattle man!”

VO: The buyer convinced Riaan to spend R100 000 on cattle to sweeten the deal and secure the sale of the farm.

RIAAN: Toe se hy vir my daai beeste wat jy nou moet kry – ek kan goedkoop beeste hier in Wes Transvaal kry.
ENGLIHSH: Then he said to me, that cattle that you have to get – I can get cheap cows here in the Western Transvaal.

VO: Riaan was sent this invoice and was told that the cattle would be transported from Christiana to his farm in Limpopo.

RIAAN: Hy bel my aanhoudend – hy se hulle wag – die beeste is gelaai – en dis ‘n lang pad – //. Ek plaas toe die R100 000 oor//
ENGLISH: He kept on phoning me – saying they’re waiting, the cattle has been loaded. And it’s long road…. I then transferred the R100 000 over.

VO: But the cattle never arrived and the money - was gone.

Meanwhile, Bennie Smit was contacted a week later. He and his wife were selling their sheep farm in the Northern Cape. They had invested their life savings in growing their herd.

BENNIE: Vir ons was dit net beter om die skaap aan te koop, om ons kudde meer te maak, en as ons geld nodig het dan vat ons 10 of 15 of 20 skape – ons vat dit veiling toe en dan het ons geld.
ENGLISH: It was just better for us buy more sheep to increase our herd, and if we need money, then we take 10 or 15 or 20 sheep and we take it to an auction and then we had money!

VO: The sale would include 318 of his sheep valued at R320 000. With the deal moving fast - the new owner wanted to move the sheep off the farm, to make room for his so-called cattle.

BENNIE: ek se man jy’t geteken, die geld is in – wanneer wil jy begin skuif? Sondag oggend, 07.00 toe is die loerie daar om die skape te laai.
ENGLISH: I said, man, you’ve signed, the money is in – when do you want to start moving? Sunday morning 07.00 the truck was there to load the sheep.

VO: Needless to say, Bennie’s money didn’t materialise.

BENNIE: jou skape is weg – jou inkomste is weg // daar is niks , daar is sweet bugger all niks – en jy kan nou niks aan die ou doen nie – want hy is nou soos ‘n skim.
ENGLISH: Your sheep are gone. Your income is gone. There’s nothing, there’s sweet bugger all nothing. And you can’t do anything to the guy because he’s like a shadow.

LINK: With no money in the bank – the livestock is gone, the phone is off the hook – the friendly old oom? He’s disappeared into thin air.

VO: But the ID number used in the sale agreements led us to a Jan Venter from Aliwal North in the Eastern Cape.

DEVI: Are you a farmer?
VENTER: yes, I am.
DEVI: Are you behind all the stock theft scams that’s been going on?
VENTER: Oh! Is that what it’s about? // He also tried to buy my farm at some stage // But I don’t know his real name.

VO: After the failed attempt to steal from him, the scamster started posing as Jan Venter – using his ID & VAT registration details to scam other farmers.

Jan started getting calls from all over South Africa.

VENTER: that’s when I realised this was quite a large operation, not just a case of trying to steal my cattle, it was getting wider and wider.

VO: So why were these farmers so easily conned? Well - the paper work checked out, the seemingly legitimate Proof of Payments arrived as promised and they all had lengthy discussions with a convincing older farmer.

BENNIE: Daar’s niks verdags aan die man dat jy kan se dit klink nie vir my lekker nie – want as jy vir hom iets vra dan weet hy daarvan – hy’t sy huiswerk gedoen – hy’t dit gedoen van A tot Z
ENGLISH: There was nothing suspicious about the man that you could say it didn’t sound right, because if you asked him something – then he knew about it. He does his homework – he did it from A to Z.

VO: Interested to know if Riaan & Bennie were speaking to same conartist, we played them audio recordings, made by others, who also had runs-in, with the Fake Jan Venter.

BENNIE & WIFE: Dis hy – Dis Jan Venter, dis hy – dis Jan Venter
- Dis hy, dis sy stem.
ENGLISH: That’s him – That’s Jan Venter. That’s him – that’s Jan Venter
- That’s him – that’s his voice.
RIAAN: 100% - Dit is Jan Venter
ENGLISH: 100%, that’s Jan Venter
DEVI: “Jan Venter”
RIAAN: Jan Venter
ENGLISH: Jan Venter

VO: Surprisingly, the cellphone numbers used by the scamster were traced to Kroonstad Prison in the Free State.

Shockingly, it’s not unusual for criminals to have access to cellphones. In 2014 , we exposed this alarming trend – we showed our evidence to correctional services spokesperson Manelisi Wolela.

UPSOUND – WATERKLOOF 4
DEVI: Are cellphone allowed in prison.
WOLELA: NO….

VO: We spoke to an ex-convict with contacts currently doing time in South African prisons.

DEVI: How do they get the phones?
JACO: In most cases you’d use a runner – you’d have some one meet the guy at court and gives him the phone and then ups the phone – they call it xxx – he wraps it in plastic and he use Vaseline to hide it between him //At other times you’d use a warden if you want a new phone.

VO: It’s not just about having access to the outside world – convicted criminals are running elaborate scams from inside.

JACO: If you have a fast enough phone you can do everything // There is a lot of scams like that the guys use – it can be cattle, it can be poultry – it can be a flat to rent… // any commodity that can be moved basically.

VO: We managed to get a new number used by the Fake Jan Venter – he was in the middle of trying to con yet another farmer in the Northern Cape.

Posing as the attorneys handling the so-called farm sale we called the number to see if the voice was the same.

CROOK: Hello, hoe gaan dit daar?
ENGLISH: Hello, how is it going there?
DEVI: Is this Jan?
CROOK: Wie praat nou? INT1 M1
ENGLISH: Who’s speaking now?

VO: Sounds the same to us…but notice what happens when he speaks English.

DEVI: When are you going to lodge the deposit?
CROOK: Come again Ma’am…. // When can I do what?
DEVI: Can you lodge the deposit…
CROOK: No, no, no….INT1 M2

VO: Did you also hear the accent change?

DEVI: Where are you at the moment?
CROOK: I’m in Nelspruit Ma’am. INT1 M3

VO: Wrong.....

DEVI: you’re in Kroonstad Prison right now aren’t you?
CROOK: // you must not even do any allegation against me.// CUT CALL

VO: It seems we struck a nerve….

This suspect has been convicted of stock theft & fraud, he is currently standing trial in 8 other stock theft cases – besides the new cases we have uncovered.

Our investigation revealed that he’s not operating alone...

Some sale agreements were scanned at the Tswelopele Municipality in Bultfontein, in the Free State.

LINK: //We’ve linked a municipality staff member to the scam – he’s got some explaining to do…

DEVI: I’m looking for Kibiti?
DEVI: Your email has been linked to scam – have you scanned any purchase and sale agreements//?
KIBITI: No, no, no…. INT1 M1
DEVI: that’s the scanning system – if you didn’t do it – who did it?
KIBITI: Someone else
DEVI: Who has access? Is it password protected?
KIBITI: No…INT1 M5

VO: Funny that – watch as Kibiti logs on to his PC using a password…

DEVI: you put a password
KIBITI: we have two Its
DEVI: is it password protected
KIBITI: ah-ah… (no)
DEVI: But you put a password now? Is it the same password for everybody?
KIBITI: No – it’s not the same…. INT1 M10

VO: Realising, we were onto him…he changed tactics….

KIBITI: Let me contact my lawyer – you are asking me too many questions… INT1 M12

VO: We were called to the Municipal Manager’s office, but when we got there things took a turn.

UPSOUND SCUFFLE…. Don’t touch me…

VO: It seems the municipal manager and her staff were not interested in hearing the allegations….

UPSOUND: Can you get out of my institution…

VO: Later that same day the police’s Cyber Crime Unit seized Kibiti’s computer.

But the municipality is not the only link – it appears that a second accomplice sends out the fake proof of payments.

They are sent from this email address: mampanepule65@gmail.com. It’s linked via social media to Pule Mampane – a computer repairer from Theunissen just 45 minutes from the Municipality.

Unable locate a home address for Pule, we got hold of him on the phone.

DEVI: Your email address… you have been sending fake proof of payment…
PULE: No… no…
DEVI: yes, you!
PULE: Wrong number
DEVI: No, same number – this is your instagram email address
PULE: no, no, it’s not me….

VO: But it is him… the police have subsequently linked him to the suspect in Kroonstad Prison.

LINK: The buck stops with correctional services – the man is in prision committing a crime, under their roof, on their watch while taxpayers pay for his upkeep.

BENNIE: Jammer om dit te se maar hulle is properly sleg – hulle doen nie hulle werk nie.
ENGLISH: Sorry to say it, but they are properly useless – they are not doing their work!

VO: The Department of Correctional Services declined our requests for an interview stating: “…the participation of DCS may hamper the administration of justice.”

But even after raising the illegal use of cellphones in prisons with the Department – it seems that no action has been taken - we were able to get these pictures from inside South African prisons just this week.

BENNIE: Hoeveel van ons mense is slag offers hier buite – jy word gemanipuleer deur mense wat binne in tronke sit – jy kan nie glo dat dit met in ons in hierdie nuwe Suid Afrika gebeur nie.
ENGLISH: How many of us are victims here outside? You are manipulated by people that are sitting inside prisons! You can’t believe that it’s happening to us in this new South Africa.


PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Livestock theft has been taken to a whole new level with a sophisticated scam being operated, straight from within a Free State Prison.

PROMO 2
VO: A sophisticated conman targets farmers using fake property deals as a decoy to steel livestock.

BENNIE: jou skape is weg – jou inkomste is weg // daar is niks , daar is sweet bugger all niks.

VO: We expose the syndicate behind the con.


PROMO 3
VO: From identity theft, to fake proof of payments – a new scam takes livestock theft to the next level.

BENNIE: jy word gemanipuleer deur mense wat binne in tronke sit – jy kan nie glo dat dit met in ons in hierdie nuwe Suid Afrika gebeur nie.

But one scamster has been running a sophisticated operation, stealing from desperate farmers - seemingly from within his cell - inside Kroonstad Prison. From cattle, to sheep - livestock theft has been taken to a whole new level. Carte Blanche investigates this cunning conman. Script: STRUCTURE VO: Times are tough in the South African farming industry. BENNIE: Ons sukkel op hierdie stadium jy kan se om kop bo water te bly. ENGLISH: We are battling at this stage, you can say to keep our heads above water. LINK: Economic and climatic conditions have resulted in more and more farms up for sale – but desperate times often opens to the door to conartists. VO: At least 15 farmers have been scammed with fake deals totalling close to R2.5 million. Bennie Smit and Riaan Lotz were contacted by a man wanting to buy their farms. RIAAN: Hy het glad nie geknibble oor die prys nie. ENGLISH: He didn’t argue about the price at all. UPSOUND AUDIO RECORDING CLIP…. Man, I am looking for any farm, but it has to be a running concern, because look I am a cash buyer. BENNIE: Daar’s nie twee stories – dis ‘n kontant koper. Joh dit kan nie beter gaan nie. ENGLISH: There’s no two stories - it’s a cash buyer. Joh! It can’t go any better! RIAAN: Hy’t gese hy is Jan Venter – hy is ‘n boer hy het voerkrale – hy is van Nelspruit en hy stel belang in my plaas. ENGLISH: He said he is Jan Venter – he’s farmer with feeding pens. He’s from Nelspruit and he’s interested in my farm. VO: Riaan & Bennie would only learn later on that the scam wasn’t actually about the sale of the farms – it was just a decoy. After a year on the market – Riaan was happy with the offer for his game farm in Limpopo. But it wasn’t a done deal - the buyer wanted livestock on the farm. RIAAN: Ek het hom probeer oorreed om te se jy kan die plaas as ‘n lopend saak koop, want daar is baie die wild op dit // – maar hy’t aanhou se – ek is ‘n bees man INT1 M7 ENGLISH: I tried to convince him that he can buy the farm as a going concern because there is a lot of game on it. But he kept saying – “I am a cattle man!” VO: The buyer convinced Riaan to spend R100 000 on cattle to sweeten the deal and secure the sale of the farm. RIAAN: Toe se hy vir my daai beeste wat jy nou moet kry – ek kan goedkoop beeste hier in Wes Transvaal kry. ENGLIHSH: Then he said to me, that cattle that you have to get – I can get cheap cows here in the Western Transvaal. VO: Riaan was sent this invoice and was told that the cattle would be transported from Christiana to his farm in Limpopo. RIAAN: Hy bel my aanhoudend – hy se hulle wag – die beeste is gelaai – en dis ‘n lang pad – //. Ek plaas toe die R100 000 oor// ENGLISH: He kept on phoning me – saying they’re waiting, the cattle has been loaded. And it’s long road…. I then transferred the R100 000 over. VO: But the cattle never arrived and the money - was gone. Meanwhile, Bennie Smit was contacted a week later. He and his wife were selling their sheep farm in the Northern Cape. They had invested their life savings in growing their herd. BENNIE: Vir ons was dit net beter om die skaap aan te koop, om ons kudde meer te maak, en as ons geld nodig het dan vat ons 10 of 15 of 20 skape – ons vat dit veiling toe en dan het ons geld. ENGLISH: It was just better for us buy more sheep to increase our herd, and if we need money, then we take 10 or 15 or 20 sheep and we take it to an auction and then we had money! VO: The sale would include 318 of his sheep valued at R320 000. With the deal moving fast - the new owner wanted to move the sheep off the farm, to make room for his so-called cattle. BENNIE: ek se man jy’t geteken, die geld is in – wanneer wil jy begin skuif? Sondag oggend, 07.00 toe is die loerie daar om die skape te laai. ENGLISH: I said, man, you’ve signed, the money is in – when do you want to start moving? Sunday morning 07.00 the truck was there to load the sheep. VO: Needless to say, Bennie’s money didn’t materialise. BENNIE: jou skape is weg – jou inkomste is weg // daar is niks , daar is sweet bugger all niks – en jy kan nou niks aan die ou doen nie – want hy is nou soos ‘n skim. ENGLISH: Your sheep are gone. Your income is gone. There’s nothing, there’s sweet bugger all nothing. And you can’t do anything to the guy because he’s like a shadow. LINK: With no money in the bank – the livestock is gone, the phone is off the hook – the friendly old oom? He’s disappeared into thin air. VO: But the ID number used in the sale agreements led us to a Jan Venter from Aliwal North in the Eastern Cape. DEVI: Are you a farmer? VENTER: yes, I am. DEVI: Are you behind all the stock theft scams that’s been going on? VENTER: Oh! Is that what it’s about? // He also tried to buy my farm at some stage // But I don’t know his real name. VO: After the failed attempt to steal from him, the scamster started posing as Jan Venter – using his ID & VAT registration details to scam other farmers. Jan started getting calls from all over South Africa. VENTER: that’s when I realised this was quite a large operation, not just a case of trying to steal my cattle, it was getting wider and wider. VO: So why were these farmers so easily conned? Well - the paper work checked out, the seemingly legitimate Proof of Payments arrived as promised and they all had lengthy discussions with a convincing older farmer. BENNIE: Daar’s niks verdags aan die man dat jy kan se dit klink nie vir my lekker nie – want as jy vir hom iets vra dan weet hy daarvan – hy’t sy huiswerk gedoen – hy’t dit gedoen van A tot Z ENGLISH: There was nothing suspicious about the man that you could say it didn’t sound right, because if you asked him something – then he knew about it. He does his homework – he did it from A to Z. VO: Interested to know if Riaan & Bennie were speaking to same conartist, we played them audio recordings, made by others, who also had runs-in, with the Fake Jan Venter. BENNIE & WIFE: Dis hy – Dis Jan Venter, dis hy – dis Jan Venter - Dis hy, dis sy stem. ENGLISH: That’s him – That’s Jan Venter. That’s him – that’s Jan Venter - That’s him – that’s his voice. RIAAN: 100% - Dit is Jan Venter ENGLISH: 100%, that’s Jan Venter DEVI: “Jan Venter” RIAAN: Jan Venter ENGLISH: Jan Venter VO: Surprisingly, the cellphone numbers used by the scamster were traced to Kroonstad Prison in the Free State. Shockingly, it’s not unusual for criminals to have access to cellphones. In 2014 , we exposed this alarming trend – we showed our evidence to correctional services spokesperson Manelisi Wolela. UPSOUND – WATERKLOOF 4 DEVI: Are cellphone allowed in prison. WOLELA: NO…. VO: We spoke to an ex-convict with contacts currently doing time in South African prisons. DEVI: How do they get the phones? JACO: In most cases you’d use a runner – you’d have some one meet the guy at court and gives him the phone and then ups the phone – they call it xxx – he wraps it in plastic and he use Vaseline to hide it between him //At other times you’d use a warden if you want a new phone. VO: It’s not just about having access to the outside world – convicted criminals are running elaborate scams from inside. JACO: If you have a fast enough phone you can do everything // There is a lot of scams like that the guys use – it can be cattle, it can be poultry – it can be a flat to rent… // any commodity that can be moved basically. VO: We managed to get a new number used by the Fake Jan Venter – he was in the middle of trying to con yet another farmer in the Northern Cape. Posing as the attorneys handling the so-called farm sale we called the number to see if the voice was the same. CROOK: Hello, hoe gaan dit daar? ENGLISH: Hello, how is it going there? DEVI: Is this Jan? CROOK: Wie praat nou? INT1 M1 ENGLISH: Who’s speaking now? VO: Sounds the same to us…but notice what happens when he speaks English. DEVI: When are you going to lodge the deposit? CROOK: Come again Ma’am…. // When can I do what? DEVI: Can you lodge the deposit… CROOK: No, no, no….INT1 M2 VO: Did you also hear the accent change? DEVI: Where are you at the moment? CROOK: I’m in Nelspruit Ma’am. INT1 M3 VO: Wrong..... DEVI: you’re in Kroonstad Prison right now aren’t you? CROOK: // you must not even do any allegation against me.// CUT CALL VO: It seems we struck a nerve…. This suspect has been convicted of stock theft & fraud, he is currently standing trial in 8 other stock theft cases – besides the new cases we have uncovered. Our investigation revealed that he’s not operating alone... Some sale agreements were scanned at the Tswelopele Municipality in Bultfontein, in the Free State. LINK: //We’ve linked a municipality staff member to the scam – he’s got some explaining to do… DEVI: I’m looking for Kibiti? DEVI: Your email has been linked to scam – have you scanned any purchase and sale agreements//? KIBITI: No, no, no…. INT1 M1 DEVI: that’s the scanning system – if you didn’t do it – who did it? KIBITI: Someone else DEVI: Who has access? Is it password protected? KIBITI: No…INT1 M5 VO: Funny that – watch as Kibiti logs on to his PC using a password… DEVI: you put a password KIBITI: we have two Its DEVI: is it password protected KIBITI: ah-ah… (no) DEVI: But you put a password now? Is it the same password for everybody? KIBITI: No – it’s not the same…. INT1 M10 VO: Realising, we were onto him…he changed tactics…. KIBITI: Let me contact my lawyer – you are asking me too many questions… INT1 M12 VO: We were called to the Municipal Manager’s office, but when we got there things took a turn. UPSOUND SCUFFLE…. Don’t touch me… VO: It seems the municipal manager and her staff were not interested in hearing the allegations…. UPSOUND: Can you get out of my institution… VO: Later that same day the police’s Cyber Crime Unit seized Kibiti’s computer. But the municipality is not the only link – it appears that a second accomplice sends out the fake proof of payments. They are sent from this email address: mampanepule65@gmail.com. It’s linked via social media to Pule Mampane – a computer repairer from Theunissen just 45 minutes from the Municipality. Unable locate a home address for Pule, we got hold of him on the phone. DEVI: Your email address… you have been sending fake proof of payment… PULE: No… no… DEVI: yes, you! PULE: Wrong number DEVI: No, same number – this is your instagram email address PULE: no, no, it’s not me…. VO: But it is him… the police have subsequently linked him to the suspect in Kroonstad Prison. LINK: The buck stops with correctional services – the man is in prision committing a crime, under their roof, on their watch while taxpayers pay for his upkeep. BENNIE: Jammer om dit te se maar hulle is properly sleg – hulle doen nie hulle werk nie. ENGLISH: Sorry to say it, but they are properly useless – they are not doing their work! VO: The Department of Correctional Services declined our requests for an interview stating: “…the participation of DCS may hamper the administration of justice.” But even after raising the illegal use of cellphones in prisons with the Department – it seems that no action has been taken - we were able to get these pictures from inside South African prisons just this week. BENNIE: Hoeveel van ons mense is slag offers hier buite – jy word gemanipuleer deur mense wat binne in tronke sit – jy kan nie glo dat dit met in ons in hierdie nuwe Suid Afrika gebeur nie. ENGLISH: How many of us are victims here outside? You are manipulated by people that are sitting inside prisons! You can’t believe that it’s happening to us in this new South Africa. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Livestock theft has been taken to a whole new level with a sophisticated scam being operated, straight from within a Free State Prison. PROMO 2 VO: A sophisticated conman targets farmers using fake property deals as a decoy to steel livestock. BENNIE: jou skape is weg – jou inkomste is weg // daar is niks , daar is sweet bugger all niks. VO: We expose the syndicate behind the con. PROMO 3 VO: From identity theft, to fake proof of payments – a new scam takes livestock theft to the next level. BENNIE: jy word gemanipuleer deur mense wat binne in tronke sit – jy kan nie glo dat dit met in ons in hierdie nuwe Suid Afrika gebeur nie. An opportunity to throw the spotlight on the weaknesses with in Correctional Services - I did the Waterkloof 4 story at least 3 years ago when we showed the extent of cellphones in prisons - but it's gone next level with criminals not only having access to the outside world - but are running extensive cons from inside.
metadata.Summary: Times are tough in the farming industry. The economy and the climate has taken it’s toll on many farmers, with more and more farms up for sale. A conman is exploiting their desperation – pretending to buy farms using stolen details and fake proof of payments only to steal their livestock. Sound like a straightforward con? But there’s twist. The crook is already behind bars – he’s running the scam from inside the Kroonstad Prison.
metadata.Further information: THE CON The Farming community has become the playground of a very inventive conman. He’s knowledgable and sounds like older, Afrikaans farmer who knows the business and speaks the lingo. The Conman responds to For Sale ads for farms and livestock. He makes an offer, signs the offer to purchases with comprehensive details and sends through a proof of payment. He’ll send through a foreman to inspect the farm while the deal is going on making it seem legit. Then he’ll want to move the livestock and starts making arrangements. Often he’s dealing with farmers in areas that have bad cellphone reception or where the farmers aren’t physically on the land. A livestock transporter will arrive and make off with the livestock – it’s either sold at an auction or to butchery or another farmer. Before you know you know it, the animals are gone and there is no sign of the money in your bank account. The foreman & transporter are NOT part of the con – they have ALSO been conned! They don’t get payment for their services and are left out of pocket. Farmers have been targeted across SA – from the Free State, to the Northern Cape to the Eastern Cape. If you look at the proof of payments – you can find problems with it if you compare it to an original one from the bank – issues around layout and spelling. SO WHO IS THE CON? Well he uses different aliases – usually the name of the previous farmer he scammed because during the sale process he would have gotten all the details – ID’s, contact addresses, etc. So when the new mark dues his due diligence – there will be a legitimate person, who is in the farming industry by that name usually with other properties on their name. The con is a man by the name of Joseph Nguro. He grew up on farms in the Free State and is currently serving a sentence in the Kroonstad Prison for fraud and stock theft. His old MO was to physically cut fences and steal live stock. There is another 9 cases using his original MO currently running in court where he is linked. With his new MO there are 27 cases being investigated linked back to Joseph. The police’s Stock Theft Unit is making progress but they are frustrated with Correctional Services – the prisoner is able to run an elaborate con from his jail cell using mobile phones. HOW DO WE DO IT? We have access to a number of voice recordings of the con making arrangement to buy the farms and move the animals. All the recording from the different scams are the same voice. We will be able to shoot re-enactment of the animals being loaded – so visually we’ll have creative overlay. AND THEN ☺ We can post an ad for a farm with livestock – pretending that my father passed away and that I need to sell quite quickly. That way we’ll get our own recordings, and we’ll be able to trace the cell numbers ourselves to link it back to the suspect. We could even get Devi to call him and call him out on the con. CASE STUDIES CASE STUDY 1 Bennie Smit from Stompiesfontein in the Calvinia District received an offer to purchase his farm and the livestock on the farm. His estate agent and lawyers said it looked legit. The new buyer wanted to move the sheep to another farm. 318 sheep was loaded. The value R318k – it was sold to a butcher in the Free State who says all the animals have been slaughtered. (We don’t need to go Calvinia – we can meet him Wolseley – it’s about 2 hours from Cape Town) CASE STUDY 2 Gert Bekker got an offer to purchase from Jan Hendrik Potgieter. He pretend to buy the farm, made appointments to sign contracts, sent fake EFT-payments to Bekker and his lawyers and then started to move livestock, by the time Bekker realize that the proof of payment was fake, the livestock was long gone, but luckily in time to stop another shipment of livestock being loaded by the crooks This is his story: We had daily conversations. In short he decide to buy our farm as a running business with the exclusion of some of the livestock. Becker Bergh and More were assign to draw up the contracts for the running business and via e-mail the documents were sign. He (Jan Hendrik Potgieter) make arrangements to come to Upington on the 4th of July to sign the original contracts. On 29th June 2017 he send proof of payments for the livestock (R1871 880.00) to me, and for the farm (R24 463 084.96) to Becker Bergh and More. He organize transport, with a local transporter, for the livestock on the 29th June and 1st July. When the money was not made available to my bank by the 1st of July, I suspect something was wrong and stop the second shipment of livestock. CASE STUDY 3 THE REAL Jan Hendrik Potgieter was almost scammed in June. He dealt with the same conman pretending to be a Benjamin Nel. The crook arranged for cattle to be loaded – but fortunately for the real Jan – the auctioneers picked up something was amiss and they traced the animals back to him. His son-in-law has started a group for affected farmers and can give a good overview of the scam. CASE STUDY 4 Raymond Daniels got offered a job as the foreman in one of these cons – he packed up his house, resigned from his job because of the brilliant offer he was made. He drove thousands of kilometres to the so-called farm and helped finalise arrangements for the transportation of livestock. He was left out of pocket, out of a job and had a lot of explaining to do to the angry farmer who initially thought he was part of con but only realised later Raymond was also a victim.
